name: The Mountain Goats
label: Merge
lede: One man, a Panasonic boombox and a psych-ward day job in Southern California, then thirty-odd years later a four-piece band singing about wrestlers, goths, Dungeons & Dragons and his own stepfather to rooms full of people who know every word.

eras.title: Songs into a boombox in Claremont
eras.text: John Darnielle had already been through a meth habit in Portland and was working in a psychiatric hospital when he started taping songs straight into a cassette boombox. The Mountain Goats were whatever he recorded that week, released on tapes and 7-inches through tiny labels like Shrimper.

years.h: Taboo VI: The Homecoming, a Shrimper cassette
years.p: Dennis Callaci's Shrimper label puts out John Darnielle's first Mountain Goats tape, Taboo VI: The Homecoming. The name comes from Screamin' Jay Hawkins's song Yellow Coat.
years.xp: Darnielle, born in 1967, had lived in Portland, Oregon, after high school, where by his own account he was addicted to intravenous methamphetamine. By now he was working on the psychiatric ward at Metropolitan State Hospital in Norwalk, California, and studying Classics and English at Pitzer College.

years.h: Zopilote Machine, with the Bright Mountain Choir
years.p: The first full Mountain Goats album, on Ajax, and the only one with the whole Bright Mountain Choir, an all-girl reggae group. Its bassist, [[Rachel Ware|a3c4ff1f-ab55-4cd9-b914-ab69fa2b7ab8]], plays with John Darnielle live until 1995.

years.h: John Darnielle swears off swearing in his songs
years.p: John Darnielle announces a vow to clean profanity out of his Mountain Goats songs, hoping for a more hopeful reception.

eras.title: The last boombox record
eras.text: Full Force Galesburg, a wedding in Iowa, then a long quiet stretch. In 2002 Darnielle made the boombox album to end all boombox albums and, the same year, walked into a real studio with a full band for a real label.

years.h: John Darnielle marries Lalitree Chavanothai in Colo, Iowa
years.p: John Darnielle and Lalitree Chavanothai marry in Colo, Iowa. Mountain Goats output slows for the next few years.

years.h: All Hail West Texas, all on the Panasonic boombox
years.p: Emperor Jones releases All Hail West Texas, recorded in 2001 on John Darnielle's Panasonic RX-FT500. The cover promises fourteen songs about seven people.
years.xp:
The Best Ever Death Metal Band in Denton opens it, and Jenny introduces a character who comes back 21 years later on Jenny from Thebes. Darnielle calls it the culmination of his lo-fi style.

When outtakes leaked, Wikipedia says, he destroyed fifteen more recordings from the period rather than risk them getting out.

years.h: Tallahassee: 4AD, a studio and the Alpha couple
years.p: The first Mountain Goats album made with a full band in a studio, for 4AD. It follows the Alpha couple, a marriage going bad in a house in Florida.
years.xp: No Children, the couple's poisonous duet with themselves, kept finding new audiences for two decades and had a second life on TikTok in the 2020s.

years.h: Peter Hughes joins The Mountain Goats for good
years.p: [[Peter Hughes|012931a2-fa02-425b-8f23-908f73eb7b85]], who had played bass on tours after Rachel Ware left, becomes a full member in 2002.

eras.title: Telling on himself
eras.text: Darnielle moved to Durham, North Carolina, and stopped hiding behind characters. With producer John Vanderslice he made one record about his speed years and one about the stepfather who beat him, and a band grew up around him: Hughes, then Jon Wurster of Superchunk.

years.h: John Darnielle moves to Durham, North Carolina
years.p: John Darnielle settles in Durham, North Carolina, a short drive from Merge's home in Chapel Hill and later the band's base.

years.h: We Shall All Be Healed: the meth years
years.p: John Darnielle's first openly autobiographical Mountain Goats album, and first with producer John Vanderslice, is about his friends addicted to methamphetamine in Portland, moved to Pomona, California.

years.h: The Sunset Tree: John Darnielle's abusive stepfather
years.p: John Darnielle's 4AD album about growing up in Claremont with a stepfather who abused him. Its song This Year becomes a live staple.
years.xp: Produced by John Vanderslice. The same stepfather took young Darnielle to pro wrestling at the Grand Olympic Auditorium in Los Angeles, which is where Beat the Champ comes from ten years later.

years.h: Superchunk's Jon Wurster takes the drum stool
years.p: Jon Wurster of [[Superchunk|61653550-fd9b-4401-8248-44f2d064d384]] joins The Mountain Goats on drums for the last leg of the Get Lonely tour and stays.

years.h: Heretic Pride with Franklin Bruno and St. Vincent
years.p: The Mountain Goats' Heretic Pride features [[Franklin Bruno|e215dcc5-4193-493c-ac7a-436625bcf4e9]] and Annie Clark, a.k.a. [[St. Vincent|5334edc0-5faf-4ca5-b1df-000de3e1f752]], alongside John Darnielle, Peter Hughes and Jon Wurster.

years.h: John Darnielle's 33⅓ book on Black Sabbath is a novel
years.p: John Darnielle's entry in the 33⅓ series, Black Sabbath: Master of Reality, is a novella about a teenager in a psychiatric facility, not music criticism.

years.h: Moon Colony Bloodbath: organ harvesting on the Moon
years.p: A limited vinyl EP from The Mountain Goats, conceived as a concept record about organ-harvesting colonies on the Moon.

years.h: TV debut on The Colbert Report, for a fan named Stephen
years.p: Stephen Colbert, a self-declared fan, books The Mountain Goats for their first TV appearance. They play Psalms 40:2 from The Life of the World to Come.
years.xp: The Life of the World to Come, out that month on 4AD, has twelve songs each named for a Bible verse. Ten years later, in July 2019, Colbert sang This Year with the band on The Late Show.

eras.title: Merge, wrestlers and goths
eras.text: Signing with Merge put the band in its own backyard. The records got stranger and more specific (a wrestling album, an album with no guitars, a Dungeons & Dragons album) while Darnielle became a novelist on the side.

years.h: The Mountain Goats sign to Merge Records
years.p: After eight years on 4AD, The Mountain Goats sign with Chapel Hill's Merge Records, home of Jon Wurster's other band, Superchunk.

years.h: All Eternals Deck, the first Mountain Goats album on Merge
years.p: The Mountain Goats' first album for Merge, All Eternals Deck, arrives in March 2011.

years.h: Transcendental Youth adds Matthew E. White's horns
years.p: The Mountain Goats' Transcendental Youth brings in a horn section arranged by Matthew E. White.

years.h: Merge puts All Hail West Texas on vinyl for the first time
years.p: Merge reissues the 2002 boombox album with seven unreleased songs and an 1,800-word essay by John Darnielle. Pitchfork calls it Best New Reissue.

years.h: Wolf in White Van gets a National Book Award nod
years.p: John Darnielle's first novel, about a disfigured man who runs a mail-order role-playing game, is nominated for the National Book Award.

years.h: Beat the Champ: a whole album about pro wrestlers
years.p: The Mountain Goats sing about the wrestlers John Darnielle watched as a kid. Multi-instrumentalist Matt Douglas plays on it and becomes a full member.

years.h: John Darnielle writes Rian Johnson a Last Jedi song
years.p: For director Rian Johnson, John Darnielle records a joke song with a title about a Jedi who eats the other Jedi's bones.

years.h: Goths, a Mountain Goats album with no guitar
years.p: John Darnielle writes about the Cure, Bauhaus and Joy Division fans he grew up with on KROQ. He leaves the guitar off entirely.
play: Andrew Eldritch Is Moving Back to Leeds

years.h: I Only Listen to the Mountain Goats podcast starts
years.p: John Darnielle and Welcome to Night Vale co-creator Joseph Fink launch a podcast going through All Hail West Texas song by song.

years.h: In League with Dragons, the Dungeons & Dragons album
years.p: The Mountain Goats' Dungeons & Dragons-inspired album, announced in January 2019 with the single Younger.

eras.title: Back to the boombox, then a bass player goes
eras.text: When the pandemic shut everything, Darnielle dug the old Panasonic out and made a tape album in days. Four more records followed in four years, then Peter Hughes, the bassist since 2002, stepped away.

years.cap: Songs for Pierre Chuvin, Merge cassette
years.h: Songs for Pierre Chuvin: the boombox, 18 years later
years.p: In lockdown, John Darnielle records ten songs straight into his Panasonic RX-FT500 for the first time since 2002. The themes come from Pierre Chuvin's book A Chronicle of the Last Pagans.

years.h: Getting Into Knives, made in Memphis
years.p: The Mountain Goats' full-band album Getting Into Knives, recorded at Sam Phillips Recording in Memphis just before lockdown.

years.h: Dark in Here, cut at FAME in Muscle Shoals
years.p: The Mountain Goats record Dark in Here at FAME Studios in Muscle Shoals, Alabama.

years.h: John Darnielle's Devil House, an Edgar Award nominee
years.p: John Darnielle's third novel, Devil House, about a true-crime writer, is nominated for an Edgar Award.

years.h: Bleed Out, an album of action-movie songs
years.p: The Mountain Goats' Bleed Out is built around the action films John Darnielle watched in the early pandemic.

years.h: Jenny from Thebes: a rock opera for a 2002 character
years.p: The Mountain Goats build a rock opera around Jenny, the woman first sung about on All Hail West Texas in 2002.

years.h: Peter Hughes leaves The Mountain Goats
years.p: After almost 30 years in and around the band, bassist Peter Hughes quits, saying he needs to look after his health and sanity.

eras.title: Off Merge, onto their own
eras.text: With a new bassist and after fifteen years on Merge, The Mountain Goats started putting records out through Cadmean Dawn. Darnielle kept writing at the same absurd pace.

years.h: Cameron Ralston becomes The Mountain Goats' bassist
years.p: Cameron Ralston joins on bass, completing a lineup of John Darnielle, Jon Wurster, Matt Douglas and Ralston.

years.h: Through This Fire Across from Peter Balkan leaves Merge
years.p: The Mountain Goats' first album after 15 years with Merge comes out on Cadmean Dawn. It started as a dream John Darnielle wrote down.

years.h: Days, another Cadmean Dawn release
years.p: The Mountain Goats release Days on Cadmean Dawn, nine months after their last album.
